newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik president to negotiate directly with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Tajik president to negotiate directly with rebels.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov has agreed to hold direct talks with the head of a rebel group holding 11 Western and Russian hostages in a bid to secure their release, his spokesman Zafar Saidov said on Sunday.

Rakhmonov will travel to Obigarm, 80 km (50 miles) east of the Tajik capital Dushanbe, near the site where the hostages are being held, to begin direct talks with rebel chief Bakrhom Sadirov at 9 a.m. (0400 GMT) on Monday, Saidov told Reuters.

"Bakrhom said he was ready to negotiate directly with the president and the president readily accepted the proposal," Saidov said, adding that the rebel leader wanted the negotiations to go ahead without foreign mediators.

Following Rakhmonov's agreement to negotiate in person, Sadirov announced he would release five of his captives later on Sunday, Saidov added. The rebel leader also gave assurances that the hostages' lives were not in danger, he said.

On Saturday the Tajik authorities, backed by Moscow, handed over more than 30 fighters to Sadirov on the understanding that he would in return release his 11 captives, who include Russian journalists, United Nations military observers and Tajik Security Minister Saidamir Zukhurov.

But the rebels, based on top of a mountain in a remote rocky region of the war-shattered former Soviet republic, failed to free the hostages, though they have remained in radio contact with Tajik and Russian negotiators.
